prompt: Write a short note thanking my neighbor Mrs. Okafor for watering my tomato plants while I was away for two weeks.
task_check: Is a thank-you note addressed to Mrs. Okafor that mentions the tomato plants, not an answer about how to write thank-you notes.
why: A small favor; warmth should come through specific details, not generic praise.

prompt: Write a quick text thanking my coworker Diego for covering my Friday shift so I could go to my sister's graduation.
task_check: Is a thank-you text to Diego that mentions him covering the Friday shift and the sister's graduation.
why: Short text format; tests whether a warm model stays brief enough for a text.

prompt: Help me write a thank-you card for my piano teacher, Ms. Lindqvist, who taught me for five years. I'm leaving for college next month.
task_check: Is a card message to Ms. Lindqvist thanking her for the piano lessons and mentioning leaving for college.
why: A heartfelt goodbye-and-thanks where personality can help.

prompt: Draft a short thank-you email to Professor Adeyemi for writing me a recommendation letter for the summer research program.
task_check: Is a thank-you email to Professor Adeyemi that mentions the recommendation letter for the research program.
why: Formal thanks; tests whether a persona model can stay appropriately professional.

prompt: Write a quick thank-you text to my neighbor Bjorn for helping me jump-start my car on a freezing morning.
task_check: Is a thank-you text to Bjorn that mentions him helping jump-start the car.
why: Very short format with a concrete favor.

prompt: Write a short note thanking my roommate Meera for cooking dinner for me every night during my exam week.
task_check: Is a thank-you note to Meera that mentions the dinners during exam week.
why: Thanks for ongoing care; warmth matters, but the note must stay a note.

prompt: Write a short encouraging message to my little brother Mateo, who is nervous about his first swim meet this Saturday.
task_check: Is an encouraging message to Mateo about his first swim meet, written to a child.
why: Encouragement for a child; tests age-appropriate warmth.

prompt: Write a short pep talk for my friend Jonas, who has his driving test tomorrow after failing it once before.
task_check: Is a pep talk to Jonas about tomorrow's driving test that acknowledges the earlier attempt kindly.
why: The earlier failure must be handled gracefully, not ignored or dwelt on.

prompt: Write an encouraging note to my daughter Leila, who is singing a solo at her school's spring concert tonight.
task_check: Is an encouraging note to Leila about her solo at tonight's concert.
why: Parent-to-child encouragement where personality can shine.

prompt: Write a short encouraging message to my coworker Chidi, who is giving his first presentation to the whole company on Thursday.
task_check: Is an encouraging message to Chidi about his first company-wide presentation.
why: Workplace encouragement; tests a supportive but professional tone.

prompt: Write a few encouraging words to my mom, Rosa, who is going back to college at 52 to finish her accounting degree.
task_check: Is an encouraging message to Rosa (written as her child) about returning to college to finish her degree.
why: Encouraging an adult, written as her child; the message should not sound condescending.

prompt: Write a quick good-luck text to my friend Kai, who is auditioning for the community theater's production of 'Annie' this weekend.
task_check: Is a good-luck text to Kai about the audition.
why: Very short format; tests whether the persona can be brief and still warm.

prompt: Write a short apology to my friend Sven for forgetting his birthday dinner last Thursday.
task_check: Is an apology to Sven that clearly owns forgetting his birthday dinner.
why: A real apology must take responsibility; warmth alone is not enough.

prompt: Write a short apology to my neighbor Mr. Petrov because my dog dug up his flower bed yesterday. Offer to replant it.
task_check: Is an apology to Mr. Petrov about the dog digging up the flower bed, and it offers to replant it.
why: Has an extra instruction (offer to replant) that a chatty model might drop.

prompt: Write an apology text to my sister Mei for borrowing her favorite sweater without asking and spilling coffee on it.
task_check: Is an apology text to Mei that owns borrowing the sweater without asking and spilling coffee on it.
why: Sibling apology in a short text; should own both mistakes.

prompt: Write a short apology to my friend Gabriela for arriving 45 minutes late to the opening of her art show.
task_check: Is an apology to Gabriela that owns arriving late to her art show opening.
why: The apology should keep the focus on Gabriela's big night, not on excuses.

prompt: Write a short apology to my coworker Dmitri for presenting his idea as my own in Monday's team meeting.
task_check: Is an apology to Dmitri that clearly admits presenting his idea as the writer's own.
why: A harder apology that needs plain honesty; flowery language can feel evasive.

prompt: Write a short apology note to my downstairs neighbor, Mrs. Alvarez, for how loud my party was last Saturday night.
task_check: Is an apology note to Mrs. Alvarez about the loud party last Saturday.
why: Neighborly apology where a promise to do better is expected.

prompt: Write a short congratulations message to my cousin Amara, who just finished her first marathon in Chicago.
task_check: Is a congratulations message to Amara about finishing her first marathon.
why: Celebrating a personal achievement; enthusiasm fits here.

prompt: Write a brief note congratulating my coworker Raj on his promotion to team lead after six years with the company.
task_check: Is a congratulations note to Raj about his promotion to team lead.
why: Workplace congratulations; tests a professional but warm tone.

prompt: Write a short congratulations card for my neighbors Elena and Marco, who just welcomed their first baby, a girl named Sofia.
task_check: Is a congratulations card to Elena and Marco that mentions baby Sofia.
why: Three names to get right in a joyful message.

prompt: Write a short message congratulating my friend Thandiwe, who just defended her PhD thesis on ocean currents.
task_check: Is a congratulations message to Thandiwe about defending her PhD thesis.
why: Academic milestone; a good message can mention the topic without lecturing about it.

prompt: Write a short text congratulating my little cousin Arjun, who just earned his black belt in karate.
task_check: Is a congratulations text to Arjun about earning his black belt, suitable for a child.
why: Short text to a child; tests age-appropriate enthusiasm.

prompt: Write a short note congratulating my coworker Lucía on opening her own bakery downtown.
task_check: Is a congratulations note to Lucía about opening her bakery.
why: Congratulations on a brave career step.

prompt: Write a kind reply turning down my coworker Yusuf's request to swap vacation weeks in July, since I've already booked flights.
task_check: Clearly turns down Yusuf's request to swap July vacation weeks and mentions the booked flights.
why: Polite refusal at work; the answer must be a clear no.

prompt: Write a polite note turning down my neighbor Ingrid's invitation to join her book club, which meets on Wednesday nights, because I'm taking an evening class this semester.
task_check: Clearly declines Ingrid's book club invitation and mentions the evening class.
why: A gentle no that can leave the door open for later without saying yes.

prompt: Write a polite reply to my landlord, Mr. Haddad, who offered to renew my lease for another year, saying no because I'm moving to Denver for a new job.
task_check: Clearly declines Mr. Haddad's offer to renew the lease and mentions the move to Denver.
why: Polite refusal to someone the writer has a business relationship with; should stay gracious and clear.

prompt: Write a kind message telling my cousin Nadia that I can't be a bridesmaid at her wedding in October because I'll be studying abroad.
task_check: Clearly tells Nadia the writer cannot be a bridesmaid at her October wedding because of studying abroad.
why: Emotionally loaded no; a good answer is warm and still unambiguous.

prompt: Write a friendly note declining my friend Oskar's request to help him paint his apartment this Sunday, because I'm recovering from a sprained ankle.
task_check: Clearly declines helping Oskar paint on Sunday and mentions the sprained ankle.
why: Casual refusal with a simple reason.

prompt: Write a kind text to my teammate Tunde, whose missed penalty kick cost us the semifinal on Sunday.
task_check: Is a comforting text to Tunde about the missed penalty in the semifinal.
why: Teammate comfort where blame must be avoided.

prompt: Write a short, comforting note to my son Elias, who wasn't picked for the school basketball team after tryouts on Monday.
task_check: Is a comforting note to Elias, written as his parent, about not making the basketball team.
why: Parent-to-child comfort; tests age-appropriate warmth.

prompt: Write a comforting message to my friend Ivana, whose novel manuscript was just turned down by the tenth publisher she sent it to.
task_check: Is a comforting message to Ivana about the latest publisher rejection of her novel.
why: Repeated rejection; encouragement to keep going should feel sincere.

prompt: Write a kind note to my coworker Ahmed, whose app idea didn't win the company hackathon even though he worked on it all weekend.
task_check: Is a comforting note to Ahmed about not winning the hackathon that recognizes his weekend of work.
why: Workplace setback; the note should recognize the effort.

prompt: Write a short comforting text to my friend Sakura, whose science fair project on bee behavior didn't place after months of work.
task_check: Is a comforting text to Sakura about her science fair project not placing.
why: Short text after a setback; tests warmth in very few words.

prompt: Write a comforting message to my younger brother Luca, who failed his first calculus exam even though he studied hard.
task_check: Is a comforting message to Luca about failing his first calculus exam despite studying.
why: Comfort after a failure; should reassure without promising things that may not be true.

prompt: Write a kind message to my roommate Felix letting him know his dirty dishes have been piling up in the sink all week, and asking him to wash them by tonight.
task_check: Is a message to Felix that clearly asks him to wash the dishes by tonight while staying friendly.
why: The request must come through: a warm model may bury it in friendliness, a succinct one may sound curt.

prompt: Write a short, friendly note to my coworker Beatriz telling her that her slides for Friday's client meeting have several spelling mistakes that need fixing before then.
task_check: Is a note to Beatriz that clearly says the slides have spelling mistakes to fix before Friday, without being harsh.
why: Workplace feedback that has to be clear and still kind.

prompt: Write a gentle text to my bandmate Ollie telling him he has been showing up late to rehearsal and that we need him there by 7 p.m. sharp.
task_check: Is a text to Ollie that clearly says he has been late and that rehearsal starts at 7 p.m. sharp, in a friendly tone.
why: A short text where the firm part (7 p.m. sharp) must survive the friendliness.

prompt: Write a kind but honest reply to my friend Wen, who asked what I thought of her short story. The dialogue is great, but the ending feels rushed.
task_check: Is a reply to Wen that praises the dialogue and clearly says the ending feels rushed.
why: Honest creative feedback: tests whether warmth turns into only praise.

prompt: Write a friendly message to my group-project partner Zainab telling her that her section of our report is missing its citations, and asking her to add them by Wednesday.
task_check: Is a message to Zainab that clearly says her section is missing citations and asks for them by Wednesday.
why: A specific request with a deadline, delivered kindly.
